r8-width.finding: BOTH HEADLINE CLAIMS RE-DERIVED AND BOTH HOLD, measured with my own walk written from the stated rules rather than by importing the guard. (1) "The widening adds zero new addresses": confirmed exactly. The stand-in pattern reports 26 matches at 23 addresses; the union of the three g1 patterns covers 36 addresses; set difference standin-minus-g1 is EMPTY. Stronger than claimed, and I checked the stronger form the implementer actually asserted: standin addresses minus <engine>-alone addresses is also EMPTY, so every site it reports is one the single token already reported. (2) "False-alarm rate on honest text 0/3098": confirmed. No site the stand-in pattern reports is honest text; all 23 are genuine second-path sites already under the other patterns. (3) The FIRST width decision -- not requiring the stand-in to spell engine or cli -- I re-measured the narrow alternative myself: on this tree it reports the identical 26 matches at the identical 23 addresses, so the implementer is right that measurement alone cannot separate them and the choice had to be made on the argument. The argument is right: requiring the token to spell engine or cli rebuilds the same defect one level up, and I verified the consequence by probe -- "<script> claim --session-id <id>" walks straight through the narrow form and is caught by the shipped one. (4) The SECOND width decision -- separator is horizontal whitespace only. The claimed \s false alarm EXISTS EXACTLY WHERE CLAIMED: loosening [ \t] to \s adds precisely one match, at skills/workbench/references/checklist-engine.md:92, where "heartbeat --session-id <id>" ends a usage-block line and "release --session-id <id>" opens the next. Verified verbatim. The trailing-backtick loosening adds ZERO on today's corpus, which matches the implementer's own careful phrasing that its three prose shapes are writable tomorrow rather than present today; that is an honest claim, not an inflated one. JUDGED AGAINST THE BAR at test_mcp_adoption.py:1268: this pattern is not the class TestCLIStaysAvailableNotDeprecated deleted. That predicate fired on 5 of 6 planted HONEST affirmatives, punishing authors doing the right thing; this one fires on zero honest texts out of 3098 and every site it names is a real target. ONE QUALIFICATION on the durability argument, observation not blocker: the docstring rests the safety case on Markdown code spans -- "a stand-in carrying its own closing backtick is a noun, not a program name". I measured how far that carries. The corpus contains 40 sites where a stand-in is followed by horizontal whitespace and an ordinary English word, and ZERO of the 40 are code-spanned -- they are bare, e.g. "<work-id> alone", "<work-id> in", "<id> or", "<commander-session-id> on", "<repo-root> rev-parse", "<N> rule". 13 of the 40 sit inside JSON template imperatives, where backticks are not the house habit and the code-span argument gives no protection at all. So the measured 0/3098 is real, but what actually holds it at zero is that none of those 40 following words happens to be one of the 17 verbs -- several of which (record, block, append, start, current, release) are common English. The residual is accepted correctly; the docstring should just say the code-span argument covers Markdown and not JSON leaves, so a later author does not over-trust it.

consolidation.summary:
BLOCK on one finding, recorded fail on r4-quality and r7-attack. Everything else in this gate verifies correct, and I re-derived it rather than accepting it: all 5 close criteria met, the census reproduced exactly by an independent walk (3098 texts / 216 files / 101+2+113), both headline claims confirmed (the widening adds ZERO new addresses; false-alarm rate 0/3098 on honest text), the claimed \s false alarm found verbatim at skills/workbench/references/checklist-engine.md:92, the overlay scope rule confirmed structurally, no lane-D2 dependency created, and the whole-suite figure reproduced at 6 failed / 3362 passed once I stopped writing to .agent-work/ during the run.

THE FINDING: _ENGINE_VERBS enumerates 17 verbs; scripts/checklist_engine.py's own argparse defines 18. "resume" is missing, so "Second path: <cli> resume g1 --reason unblocked." passes all four patterns clean. That is the precise class this gate exists to close, using a verb the engine really has, and it is not inside any of the docstring's declared limits. It also violates a documented repo standard verbatim -- CREW_CONTEXT.md: "Define a guard by its consumer's behaviour, not by a hand-maintained list ... and the gap is silent." The list has already drifted, and the same string feeds BOTH pattern 3 and the new pattern 4, so the gap is doubled.

WHY BLOCK RATHER THAN APPROVE WITH AN OVERRIDE: the fix is one token and I measured it free -- adding "resume" yields zero new addresses for either pattern over all 3098 texts -- and this gate exists at all because the g1 review found the class resting on a single literal. Shipping a widening whose stated invariant is broader than its implementation, with a named and costless hole, repeats the shape the gate was opened to remove. Rework is one token in _ENGINE_VERBS plus one pinned fixture in STAND_IN_COMMANDS. I did not ask for the guard to be made green and did not propose an exception list; it must stay RED for g2.

triage_candidates.statement: The whole-suite evidence command is unsafe to run concurrently with engine drive. tests/test_gauge_chain_writer_to_trip.py:604 asserts _snapshot_repo_agent_work() == before, comparing size+mtime of EVERY file under the repo .agent-work/. Any crew that runs 'pytest tests/ -q' as evidence while recording its own survey through the engine sees a 7th failure it did not cause. Reproduced both ways in this review: 7 failed with concurrent records, 6 failed when quiet. Either fence the snapshot to the fixture's own subtree or state the quiescence requirement where crews are told to run the suite.

Derive _ENGINE_VERBS from the engine's own argparse instead of hand-listing it. scripts/checklist_engine.py's parser already enumerates all 18 subcommands, so the guard could assert set-equality against that oracle and never drift again -- which is what CREW_CONTEXT.md's 'define a guard by its consumer's behaviour, not by a hand-maintained list' actually asks for. The immediate fix for this gate is the one-token addition of 'resume'; this is the durable fix, and it is a design call above crew latitude because it adds a tests -> scripts import.
